properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured), limitation 12, CONFIRMED with a sharper rule. Door prose crosses two quoting layers, the shell's and JSON's. `--args -` with a QUOTED heredoc delimiter stores apostrophes, double quotes, non-ASCII, $ and backticks byte-exact. A raw newline inside a JSON string is refused (exit 1, JSON's rule: write \n). An UNQUOTED delimiter silently expands $HOME into the stored text. Nothing served says to quote the delimiter
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), triage agent D, on limitation 12 of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02 ("Shell quoting. Prose needs the --args - heredoc or a file").

② PRECEDENT: ver:a-build-can-call-one-tool-from-the-shell covers "args read from stdin". Nothing recorded about prose quoting.

③ CANDIDATES: (a) the shell's single quotes break on an apostrophe, which --args - avoids; (b) JSON's own string rules (control characters, escapes) still apply under stdin; (c) the heredoc's own expansion rules alter the prose; (d) the door mangles non-ASCII.

⑤ MEASURED (0.77.0, scratch store g110; log /home/ajs7/.claude/jobs/fa666a94/tmp/triage-D/l12.log):
A. `--call add_requirement --args - <<'EOF'` with statement "It's the user's \"quoted\" note — naïve café, 日本語 ✓\nline two with $HOME and `uname` and a back\\slash": exit 0. get_node returns it byte-identical (compared in Python). (a) avoided, (d) REFUTED.
B. The same with a RAW newline inside the JSON string (quoted delimiter): exit 1, "Error: --args is not JSON: ... control character (\u0000-\u001F) found while parsing a string". (b) HOLDS: a multi-line statement must be written with \n even inside the heredoc.
C. UNQUOTED delimiter (<<EOF) with "$HOME" in the prose: exit 0, and the stored statement reads "/home/ajs7". (c) HOLDS: a silent change to the design text, with no error.
Also: B's exit 1 is the CLI's own parse error ("Error: ..."), not a tool refusal ("reflow2: `tool` refused — ..."). Both share exit 1.

⑥ CLASS: the door takes the whole argument object as one shell word or one stdin stream, so every word of design prose passes through the shell's rules and then JSON's. reflow2 owns only the second layer and the guidance. --help says only "`-` reads the object from stdin, so a script can build it with a heredoc"; it does not say to quote the delimiter or escape newlines. A prose-carrying agent therefore learns both rules by failure, or never learns the second (C produces no error). Writing the JSON to a file with the editor tool and passing `--args - < file` avoids both shell layers, and keeps the prose out of the command text a guard hook reads (limitation 20).

WHAT REFLOW2 COULD OWN (for the owner, not decided): name the quoted delimiter and \n in --help and in the planned served instructions file (req:init-installs-the-terminal-route-for-vs-code-and-update-keeps-it-current). An `--args @file` form would let a command name the file with no redirect.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: how VS Code's terminal tool passes a heredoc through (the report says it worked there); PowerShell quoting on Windows.
